answer.why: The doc comment on `SplitCandidate` (lines 100-104) still says the same thing. `coChangedPairs` in score.ts cuts each change set to labelled paths and keeps it only when `set.length >= 2 && set.length <= maxFiles`. The per-feature score in `scoreCoChange` uses `predictedPairs([...active].filter(inF), ...)` as the denominator. That counts same-scope pairs among the feature's files touched by a kept change set, and files no kept change set touched are left out. The numerator is the co-changed pairs with both files in the feature. `splitCandidates` sets `cohesion: f.precision`, so cohesion equals the feature's per-feature precision.

The README still carries this statement at lines 188-189, and `splitCandidates` in refine.ts agrees. It drops features with `f.files < MIN_SPLIT_FILES` (4), sets `cohesion: f.precision`, and sorts ascending by cohesion. Precision is the share of same-scope pairs inside the feature that were co-changed, as the doc says. One nuance: score.ts counts pairs only among files a kept change set touched, which the doc leaves out. That doesn't make the statement false.

The shown code doesn't contradict the claims about exported names, comments or string literals.

The doc still has the line at 190: `interpret: { [K in C["type"]]: (cmd, ctx) => Promise<M | void> }`. In `pure/core.ts`, `InterpretCell` now resolves to `Promise<M | readonly M[] | void>` for hand-written Cmds. The comment there says "A list is dispatched in order as follow-ups (#324)", and `followUps()` handles arrays. A `Cmd.define`d Cmd's cell returns an `Outcome` or nothing, not a Msg. So "one follow-up Msg or nothing" is no longer accurate.
